description: Server-side paging, sorting and filtering with the headless Svelte 5 grid engine. The server owns the data and returns one page plus a total count; sort, filter and page are query params sent with each request, and the engine wraps only the page it gets back, so it never sees the other rows. A request counter shows one round trip per state change, and the markup is a hand-styled <table>.

faq.question: How does the headless engine work with server-side data?
faq.answer: Keep pageIndex, pageSize, sort and the search text as your own state, watch them in an effect, and fetch a page from your API whenever they change. Hand the returned rows to createSvGrid as its data with only the core row model; it renders those rows as-is instead of sorting or paging them locally.

faq.question: How many requests does a state change cause?
faq.answer: One. The demo counts them on screen: changing the sort, typing a filter or moving to the next page each fires a single fetch with the new params.

faq.question: Where does the total row count come from?
faq.answer: From the server's response alongside the page. The demo uses it to compute the page count for the pager; the engine itself never holds more than the current page.
